title: Kalshi Just Signed Deals With the NBA and S&P Dow Jones
description: The prediction market platform announced two major partnerships, one with the NBA and another with S&P Dow Jones Indices.
seoTitle: Kalshi Just Signed Deals With the NBA and S&P Dow Jones
html:
October 26 was a busy day for Kalshi. The prediction market platform announced two major partnerships, one with the NBA and another with S&P Dow Jones Indices. Both give Kalshi something particularly valuable as prediction markets expand: access to established institutions and the credibility associated with their names.

The NBA named Kalshi and its competitor Polymarket as Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges. The agreements provide access to official league data through Sportradar, rights to use NBA branding and opportunities for promotional campaigns in the United States.

There are conditions attached. The platforms must cooperate with the league on suspicious trading investigations, restrict certain types of markets and prohibit NBA and team personnel from trading on league-related contracts. The NBA also announced an information-sharing agreement with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

Meanwhile, Kalshi’s agreement with S&P Dow Jones Indices takes the company further into traditional finance. Kalshi will be able to offer event contracts linked to S&P DJI benchmarks, settled using official index values. S&P DJI will also explore creating indices from Kalshi’s prediction market data, potentially covering economic, political and sporting events. The companies haven’t announced when these new products will launch.

From a marketing perspective, the NBA agreement is particularly significant. It gives Kalshi access to a globally recognised sports brand and official data, while placing its name alongside a major league that has historically worked with established betting operators.

The S&P DJI partnership addresses a different audience: traders and financial institutions that already rely on recognised benchmarks.

Neither agreement resolves the regulatory disputes surrounding prediction markets. But together, they show how Kalshi is trying to position itself across two closely connected industries, finance and sports.
